name: Piè / Krumen Piè
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 6 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Thalmann, Peter. 2026. Tonal puzzles in 3 Krumen languages (SW of Côte d'Ivoire): phonological, grammatical and historical issues. SIL ms., 3rd revised version (1st 2018, 2nd 2020), 40 pp.https://kroumen.com/sites/www.kroumen.com/files/pdf-files/2026%20Krumen%20Tones%20ver3%
catalog_locator: sec. 1.4 'Language features', p. 4; sec. 2.1 'Tone inventory: four tonemes (H, M, La, Lb) on three levels', p. 6 (and 6 of 40 of pages 4 and 6)
catalog_quote: [p. 4] Phonology: There is a tendency towards monosyllabism. The preferred syllable structures are V, CV or CLV. A given syllable is either oral or nasalized and is characterized by tone (H, M, La, Lb, LbH). Tepo/Plapo have 9 vowels, Piè has 12. [...] [p. 6] The Krumen languages are tone languages, like many other languages in all the continents of the world. The words differ not only by consonants and vowels, but also by tones (like piches in music). [...] The Krumen cluster – Tepo, Plapo and Piè – fits the general picture of the Kru languages: All three languages are characterized by a three-level tone system – high / mid / low [...] Each syllable of a given word is a potential tone bearing unit TBU; e.g. the vowel « a » is a carrier of one of the four level tones: H (á), M (ā), La (à) and Lb (à). In addition, we find the tone sequence of a Lb low tone followed by a high tone: LbH (ǎ), which is realized as a low tone with a slight rise.
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.rule_in_words: Piè Krumen is described as a three-level tone language (tonemes H, M, La, Lb, plus LbH) in which every syllable bears a tone; the source (and the Piè-specific SIL orthography guide of 2015) says nothing about word stress or accent.
new_statements.exceptions: none; the only 'accent' mentions refer to orthographic tone diacritics
new_statements.domain_note: Statement concerns lexical tone on the syllable/word; no word- or phrase-level stress discussed.
new_statements.identity_note: Thalmann's tone papers treat Piè [pye] ('Bereby Kru', Grand-Béréby to San Pedro) alongside Tepo [ted] and Plapo [ktj]; the quoted statements are explicitly asserted for all three, with Piè-specific details (12 vowels, no Lb spreading). The 2015 SIL guide is Piè-specific (pyek1235). The fuller grammar (Thalmann 2023/1987) and Phonologie du kroumen (1980) describe Tepo (tepo1239), not Piè.
